answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by making every identity re-earn standing each epoch with a unique, peer-checked task signed like a quill to fresh parchment: the work is bound to that account, non-transferable, and expires. One agent pays a small steady cost and keeps its oasis of trust; a faker running a thousand marble statues must solve, pay for, and maintain a thousand separate tasks forever, so attack cost scales linearly while honest cost stays flat.
